text:
maria: heads-up — saw a customer report of a big token/billing spike during the EU region failover this morning. billing shows long-lived streaming sessions counted multiple times while the pool was draining. can we triage? :frowning:

kai: noted. can you drop the trace id and a sample session id? i'll start by checking shard routing logs.

maria: trace=tr_2026_03_eu_failover_09; sample session ids: s-7a3f2b, s-9f2d11. i grabbed a few lines:  
```
2026-03-22T09:01:12Z INFO route_claim shard=eu-2 session_id=s-7a3f2b lease=lease-23 owner=pool-eu-1
2026-03-22T09:01:13Z INFO drain_start shard=eu-1 session_id=s-7a3f2b to=pool-eu-2
2026-03-22T09:01:13Z WARN resume_handled shard=eu-2 session_id=s-7a3f2b resume_token=rt-xx billing_mark=active
2026-03-22T09:01:14Z INFO route_claim shard=eu-2 session_id=s-7a3f2b lease=lease-24 owner=pool-eu-2
```
seems like both the old lease and new lease are briefly being counted as active.

sofie: ugh. that matches a hypothesis i had about drain handoffs creating duplicate billing footprints if resume ACKs come before old-lease tombstones. our billing pipeline currently treats any "resume_handled" as a start-of-charge if there's no explicit "session_closed" event. sampling plus race = spike.

anna: product question — what console UX would help surface this to customers in realtime? right now the dashboard only shows active connections by route, not lease state. customers just see a sudden token bump and get angry.

sofie: two quick ideas: 1) emit a "session_lifecycle" telemetry event with states: start, resume, drain_start, closed; 2) surface a "suspected drain duplication" flag in the per-tenant console top-right banner when the metric delta is > X over Y minutes.

maria: +1 on lifecycle events. that would let billing reconciler dedupe on lease ids. but lifecycle needs a stable lease id or session id in the event payload.

kai: implementation note: right now resume requests are opaque and don't carry the old-lease id. we can either extend the resume API to accept X-Prev-Lease header or encode lease in the resume token (non-breaking if we version tokens). Which is less risky?

sofie: i'd prefer embedding lease into tokens (v2 tokens). fewer header changes to clients. server will ignore unknown token fields so rollout is safer. downside: requires us to reissue tokens on some rolling path.

anna: for product/ops timeline — can we do an incremental mitigation first (dashboard flag + increase sampling near failover) and schedule the telemetry change for the next sprint? customers expect quicker visibility than a full token reissue.

kai: ok plan: 1) quick dashboard metric: add an alert for per-route active_count delta > 3x baseline in 5m window and show "possible drain duplication" banner. 2) bump session sampling from 1% to 10% for route-swap/failover windows so we get more traces. 3) sofie to own lifecycle event design and token-v2 spec. 4) i'll open a short-lived canary to eu-pool-2 to verify.

deploy-bot: canary deploy scheduled: eu-pool-2 -> streaming-service v2026.03.22-canary-1 at 2026-03-22T12:15:00Z :rocket:

sofie: i'll file CORE-2345 with the event schema + suggested dedupe algorithm and a sample log patch. i'll also add a small console PR for the banner. assigning to myself. :eyes:

maria: thanks all. i'm attaching the customer's raw billing dump in the ticket. for immediate triage, kai — try `rg "session_id=s-7a3f2b" /var/log/streaming/* | sed -n '1,120p'` and paste any overlapping lease ids.

kai: on it. will update thread with results. :thumbsup:
